mechanism_narrative: The continued week-to-week rise in GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS indicates broader out-of-home circulation and errand chaining, which should spill into more discretionary shopping visits and lift RETAIL_REC within four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved from -16.1 to -12.1 over the snapshot while GROCERY_PHARM rose from 0.1 to 3.6 and PARKS from -15.0 to -10.7
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS keep rising for two more weeks but RETAIL_REC does not exceed its last-4-week mean over the next 28 days, reject the spillover mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: A persistently elevated RESIDENTIAL share reflects home-centered substitution that suppresses shopping trips, so RETAIL_REC will remain below its recent average over the next four weeks unless the residential share falls materially.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL is stable around 11.3-11.9 while RETAIL_REC remains negative
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL stays at or above 11% while RETAIL_REC rises above the last 4-week average within 28 days, the home-substitution hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT improves by at least 2 percentage points week-on-week, retail access broadens with a short lag and RETAIL_REC rises in the following 1-2 weeks; without that transit improvement, no retail rebound should occur.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by at least 2 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT moved from -22.3 to -20.1 over the snapshot
failure_condition: If TRANSIT does not improve by at least 2 points week-on-week and RETAIL_REC still rises over the next 14 days, the threshold rule is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous tightening in WORKPLACES mobility and TRANSIT mobility indicates renewed access constraints or commuting frictions, which will pull RETAIL_REC downward over the next four weeks because fewer trips combine work and shopping.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both fall for two consecutive weeks

failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both weaken for two straight weeks but RETAIL_REC does not fall below its recent 4-week mean within 28 days, the constraint mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS during a mild-weather interval reallocates discretionary time toward outdoor activity and away from shopping venues, so RETAIL_REC should soften over the next one to two weeks if PARKS keeps outperforming its earlier weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above its prior 3-week average
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -15.0 and -14.7 to -10.7 in the latest week
failure_condition: If PARKS stays above its prior 3-week average for another week but RETAIL_REC does not decline within 7-14 days, the outdoor-substitution hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A positive co-movement between GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC reflects bundled shopping behavior: more routine errands create opportunities for discretionary purchases, pushing RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks when both series rise together.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM increased every week from 0.1 to 3.6 while RETAIL_REC improved from -16.1 to -12.1
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM continues rising but RETAIL_REC remains flat or falls below its last-4-week mean over the next 28 days, the bundling mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES mobility drops below the previous week's level after a short recovery, the commuter-retail channel weakens quickly and RETAIL_REC will be lower within two weeks because fewer workers pass through shopping districts.

mechanism_narrative: A joint uptick in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES signals synchronized commuting recovery, which should raise RETAIL_REC over the next month because more trip chains include shopping stops after work.
